Ozorkow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ozorków, Poland

Demolished. Ozorków, dating to the early 15th century and granted private-town rights in 1816, saw Jewish migration tied to its developing clothing industry from the late 18th century; an independent kehilla formed in 1819, growing to 50% (5,837) of the population by 1897. A ghetto established in early 1941 held nearly 6,000 Jews; its May 1942 liquidation sent 1,700-2,000 people to Chełmno, with remaining residents transferred to the Łódź Ghetto that August. This cemetery, likely established in the first half of the 19th century, is documented in a wartime Wehrmacht soldier's photograph showing several dozen ornately decorated sandstone matzevot still standing in rows. Destruction likely began during the war and continued for years afterward.
